They, however, became enraged and erected catapults against it,
and quickly battered down its wall (its walls were battered down),
and entered and plundered it,
and killed its population,
and utterly destroyed it.
Sultan Ghiyath al-Din, however, sent ambassadors to the Tatars,
and sued for peace,
and took upon himself tribute of gold, horses, livestock, and slaves.
And in this same year,
which is the year six hundred and forty of the Arabs [AH 640],
the Caliph al-Mustansir died,
after whom [reigned] al-Musta'sim for sixteen years.
This [caliph] possessed childish intelligence,
and was not capable of distinguishing good from bad.
And all his time he was engaged in playing with pigeons and watching them fly (their flights).
And when it was said to him
that the Tatars were preparing to conquer Baghdad,
just as they had conquered and destroyed other famous cities in Persia,
he would answer:
"This is our throne,
and if we do not permit them, they cannot enter."
And in this way God brought an end to the kingdom of the Abbasids in the days of this simpleton.
And in the year 1555 [of the Greeks],
[a certain] Noyan,
descended upon the region of Mayperqat, Mardin, and Edessa.
And he crossed the Euphrates,
and reached as far as the place called Haylan, which is at the gate of Aleppo.
However, he did not approach the city itself,
because the horses of the army that was with him were stricken in their feet from the dryness of the ground and the heat,
for it was in the days of summer that they had descended.
And when they had plundered those regions,
that Yasawur (Nasawur) sent to the lord of Aleppo
and demanded gold from him.
And when he gave him everything he demanded,
he returned from there.
He came and camped against Melitene,
and destroyed the crops, vineyards, and beehives.
And these Tatars killed everyone who was found outside the city.
And they sent and threatened the governor of the city,
who was Rashid al-Din,
because he had returned from Aleppo.
And that governor collected a large tribute from the people of the city:
zuzes, dinars, jewelry, and vessels of gold and silver, to the value of forty thousand gold dinars,
and paid it over.
